correctness.rationale: Conditioning on hub and rim leaves independent Bernoulli occupations at vacant rim sites. Thus leaf covariance is t² times the effective rim covariance, with rim activity t=z/(1+z) and hub activity z. The single and double marked weights leave paths on n−3 and n−6 vertices, including P₀=1. Expansion of the marked numerator gives t³+O(t⁴) and zP_{n−6}(1)+O(1) at the two ends for fixed n. Independent full-graph enumeration gives covariance −1/14400 and −1/176400 at z=1 for n=6 and n=8. From P_k=(α^{k+2}−β^{k+2})/(α−β) and A_n=α^n+β^n, the even-n ratio in (2) follows, with C_n<1−u². The bound on the occupied-hub probability q<1/16<u² at unit activity gives strict negativity for every even n≥10. At z=cφ^n, n(1−t) tends to zero, giving (α(t)/φ)^n→1 and limiting sign comparison c/(1+c)−u_*². Brackets about its unique limiting zero yield a sequence of crossings at the stated scale (choose increasingly small brackets as n grows). The finite-n covariance is a nonzero rational function without poles on positive activities, so opposite signs do entail sign-changing zeros. No uniqueness or exact crossing count follows or is claimed.
